name: Celosia

schedule.notes: Surface-sow; needs light to germinate. Bottom heat speeds it up.
Wait for warm soil and settled nights — celosia stalls and yellows in cold soil and rarely recovers.
Cut for vases when the lowest flowers on the spike are open. Holds in the field for weeks.

harvest.cues: Plume or comb is fully colored and bottom florets are just opening. Cut long stems early morning, strip lower leaves.
harvest.storageNotes: Excellent dried — hang upside down in shade, holds color for a year. Fresh stems last 10 to 14 days in water.

varieties.name: Plumosa (Feathered)
varieties.notes: Soft feather-plumes in red, gold, pink, orange. The classic 'cockscomb' substitute, easier to dry.

varieties.name: Cristata (Cockscomb)
varieties.notes: Brain-coral-shaped crested heads, dense and weighty. Statement flower.

varieties.name: Spicata (Wheat / Flamingo Feather)
varieties.notes: Narrow wheat-like spikes in pink and silver-white. Tall (3 to 4 ft), branching, productive cut flower.

notes: Truly heat-loving — don't rush it out, cool nights stunt plants permanently. Pinch when 6 in tall to force branching and more (smaller) stems for cutting. Leaves are edible cooked greens in West African cuisine.
